Dear [Madam](/person/2234)
[Macmillan](/organisation/111) published both series of the [Store House of Stories](/book/83). I do not know that the [second series](/book/96) is gone out of print, I should think they had it in stock.

If not I could lend it to you- or my own old copy of ‘the Puzzle for a curious girl’ which I inherited from my mother, and is somewhere in the house, though I cannot lay my hand on it without a search.[^1] It has a red back, and illustrations at the top of the chapters, in the style of 1810-20, I should say - but of course they may have been made for the edition.

But I should hardly think the idea or the writing were Addisonian though it is a very clever story.

It seems to me to be of a later period than Mrs Dorothy Kilner’s Jemima Placid and the ‘little gilt books’ of the ‘corner of St Paul’s Church Yard

yours sincerely

C M Yonge


[^1]: CMY had reprinted S.W., A Puzzle for a Curious Girl (London: Tabart and Harris ?1803) in A Storehouse of Stories (London: Macmillan 1870).
